specification.problem: Time-optimal synthesis of SU(2) unitaries using only rotations about two non-parallel Bloch-sphere axes with different rotation speeds; the abstract gives structural claims (three-angle parametrization, at most five concatenations when both rotation senses are allowed) but not the explicit bounds.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest useful construction: the control-set model with two axes, the generic alternating-rotation sequence parametrization, and total time as the cost. The explicit angle bounds, scaling laws, proofs, and numerical search are outside scope. The tiny instance (axes at angle alpha, speed ratio r) is an assumption.

symbols.meaning: unit rotation axes of the two controls
rotation speeds of the two controls
rotation angle of the k-th control segment

equations.label: Rotation generators
equations.description: Single-axis SU(2) rotations for the two controls, with angle alpha between the axes.
equations.justification: The abstract states rotations about two non-parallel axes; the explicit exponential form is the standard SU(2) convention, not stated in the abstract.

equations.label: Alternating sequence
equations.description: A control sequence is a concatenation of rotations about alternating axes.
equations.abstract_quote: any finite time-optimal sequence is composed at most of five control concatenations
equations.justification: The abstract speaks of concatenations of controls. Merging adjacent same-axis rotations gives the alternating form, which is an inference.
assumptions: Sign of theta_k encodes rotation sense

equations.label: Total time cost
equations.description: Time cost of a sequence, with each axis rotating at its own speed.
equations.abstract_quote: as a function of the relative rotation speed of each control
equations.justification: Distinct rotation speeds imply the duration of a segment is angle divided by speed. The explicit formula is inferred.
assumptions: Counterclockwise rotation is a negative angle, costing |theta|/Omega when allowed; with clockwise only, theta_k>=0 mod 2pi

equations.label: Time-optimal synthesis problem
equations.latex: \min_{N,\,j_1,\,\theta_k} T\quad \text{s.t. } U(\theta_1,\dots,\theta_N)=U_{target}\ \text{(up to global phase if desired)}
equations.description: Optimization problem: the shortest-time sequence realizing the target.
equations.abstract_quote: time-optimal synthesis of arbitrary unitaries in $SU(2)$
equations.justification: This is the problem the abstract names, written as a formal optimization.

equations.label: Length bound with both rotation senses
equations.description: For finite time-optimal sequences with clockwise and counterclockwise rotations allowed, at most five concatenated controls are needed.
equations.abstract_quote: any finite time-optimal sequence is composed at most of five control concatenations
equations.justification: Direct claim in the abstract. The precise counting convention is not given.

registers.name: q
registers.role: Single qubit on which the SU(2) unitary acts

steps.description: Fix the axes, angle alpha, and speed ratio r. Choose a target U_target in SU(2).
Parametrize candidate sequences as alternating rotations.
Evaluate the time cost and impose the length bound N<=5 for the two-sense case.
Solve the constrained minimization over angles, a numerical search whose angle bounds the abstract does not give.

specification.classical_postprocessing: Numerical search over the bounded angle parameters to find the minimum-time sequence; the bounds themselves are not given in the abstract.
assumptions: No scope was supplied; the chosen scope is the generic two-axis model and cost function.
The tiny instance is an arbitrary alpha and r with a target in SU(2).
The model is analyzed at the level of unitary composition; no gate-level circuit is derived.
missing_information: Explicit bounds on the three rotation angles as functions of alpha and r
Scaling laws on maximum sequence length for the clockwise-only case
The three-angle parametrization of optimal sequences
